## Why RevealJS?

- Write slides in plain-text Quarto and Markdown.
- Keep explanation, code, results, and citations together.
- Produce an interactive HTML presentation.
- Track and review the source with Git and GitHub.

## Start with Document Metadata

```yaml
---
title: "Presentation Title"
subtitle: "Introduction to Data Science | Fall 2026"
author: "Student Name"
format:
  revealjs:
    slide-number: true
    preview-links: auto
jupyter: python3
---
```

Use `#` for a section slide and `##` for an ordinary slide.

## Prefer a Focused Story

1. Motivate the topic.
2. Explain the main idea.
3. Work through a reproducible example.
4. Interpret the result.
5. Discuss limitations or common mistakes.
6. End with two or three takeaways.

## Executable Python

Use an executable code cell when the result matters. The source and its
computed output stay together on the slide:

```{python}
#| echo: true
values = [2, 3, 5, 8]
sum(values) / len(values)
```

Explain what the output means; do not leave it for the audience to infer.

## Figures from the Same Source

```{python}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Four observations used in the example"
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(range(1, 5), values)
ax.set(xlabel="Observation", ylabel="Value")
plt.show()
```

The source, computation, and resulting figure remain together and can be
reproduced during review.

## Use Images Responsibly

- Prefer figures generated from your own code.
- Use relative paths for local images.
- Include informative alternative text.
- Verify that external images may be redistributed.
- Attribute the creator and source.

Do not paste an unattributed image from a search result into the repository.

## Keep Slides Readable

- Use short statements rather than prose paragraphs.
- Avoid presenting more code than the audience can follow.
- Label tables, axes, and important quantities.
- Define unfamiliar notation and abbreviations.
- Use incremental lists only when they improve the explanation.

## Connect the Deck to the Notes

The slide deck is published separately from the book. Add a short entry to the
relevant topical chapter containing:

- the presentation title;
- the presenter's name;
- a link to the rendered slides; and
- a two- or three-sentence abstract.

You do not need to rewrite the deck as a prose section.

## Check Before Opening a Pull Request

From an active course Python environment, run:

```bash
make render-one FILE=topic/last-name-topic/index.qmd
```

Then verify the slides in a browser and inspect `git status`. Submit the source
files, not rendered HTML, caches, or notebook intermediates.

## Takeaways

- A good deck presents one coherent, technically correct story.
- Executable examples make results inspectable and reproducible.
- Interpretation and limitations matter as much as code.
- The pull request is part of the contribution and revision process.
